claim: Claude Haiku 5.5 is released for general access, and the system card reports pre-deployment evaluations in seven areas: RSP evaluations, cyber, safeguards and harmlessness, agentic safety, alignment, model welfare, and capabilities.
quote: Claude Haiku 5.5 is a new large language model from Anthropic, released for general access. In this system card, we report results from a set of pre-deployment evaluations in seven areas

claim: Haiku 5.5's knowledge cutoff date is June 2026.
quote: Haiku 5.5’s knowledge cutoff date is June 2026.

claim: Haiku 5.5 outputs text only.
quote: The model outputs text only.

claim: Claude is multilingual, typically responds in the language of the user's input, and its output quality varies by language.
quote: Claude is multilingual and typically responds in the same language as the user’s input. Output quality varies by language.

claim: Haiku 5.5 was trained on a proprietary mix of public internet data, public and private datasets, opted-in user data, and synthetic data generated by other models, then post-trained and fine-tuned toward the values in Claude's constitution.
quote: other sources, such as synthetic data generated by other models ... underwent rigorous post-training and fine-tuning aimed at making it an assistant whose behavior aligns with the values described in Claude’s constitution

claim: Unless a section says otherwise, system card evaluations were run on the final Haiku 5.5 snapshot; some sections use an earlier or alternate snapshot or run with production safeguards disabled, so those results reflect the underlying model rather than the deployed system.
quote: Some sections instead use an earlier or alternate snapshot, or run the model with its production safeguards disabled so that the results reflect the underlying model rather than the deployed system.

claim: For chemical and biological risk, Haiku 5.5 ships with the same harmful-CB misuse classifiers as Claude Opus 5 and Claude Sonnet 5, not the broader research-biology classifiers used for Claude Opus 5.5, and these classifiers have no fallback model.
quote: we have deployed the same harmful CB misuse classifiers as for our deployments of Claude Opus 5 and Claude Sonnet 5, rather than the broader research biology classifiers used for Claude Opus 5.5. These classifiers have no fallback model.

claim: For cyber misuse, Haiku 5.5 ships with blocking classifiers that target specific harmful cyber activities, are significantly narrower than the cyber safeguards on Anthropic's more capable models, and have no fallback model.
quote: we have deployed blocking classifiers targeting specific harmful cyber activities. These are significantly narrower than our cyber safeguards for our more capable models. These classifiers have no fallback model.

claim: Haiku 5.5 carries safeguards on a narrow set of frontier-LLM-development capabilities (example given: kernel development on certain ML accelerators), similar to previous models; Anthropic says they will not affect the vast majority of traditional AI or ML development, research, or general coding.
quote: a narrow set of capabilities related to developing frontier LLMs, such as kernel development on certain ML accelerators ... They will not impact the vast majority of traditional AI or ML development, research, or general coding.

claim: Blocking classifiers for conventional weapons and high-yield explosives on Haiku 5.5 behave similarly to those on previous models such as Claude Opus 5.5.
quote: Our blocking classifiers for development of conventional weapons and high-yield explosives behave similarly to those on previous models, such as Claude Opus 5.5.

claim: Unlike some of Anthropic's more capable recent models, a safeguard block on Haiku 5.5 does not fall back to any other model on first-party products or the API; behavior on other platforms and providers may differ.
quote: Unlike some of our more capable recent models, blocks on these safeguards will not fall back to any other models on our first-party products and our API. Traffic on our models via other platforms and providers may experience different behavior.

claim: The majority of Haiku 5.5 evaluations were run in-house at Anthropic, with some assessments contributed by external testers.
quote: The majority of evaluations of Claude Haiku 5.5 were run in-house at Anthropic.

claim: Anthropic states Haiku 5.5 is not at the capability frontier and is less capable than Claude Opus 5 across a large majority of the evaluations reported in the card (RSP section and the Section 8 capability evaluations).
quote: Haiku 5.5 is not at the capability frontier, and is less capable than Claude Opus 5 across a large majority of the evaluations we report.

claim: Haiku 5.5 is determined not to cross the CB-2 or Autonomy-2 RSP thresholds, but is treated as meeting the CB-1 and Autonomy-1 thresholds, with the corresponding RSP mitigations applied.
quote: we determine that Haiku 5.5 does not cross our CB-2 or Autonomy-2 RSP thresholds. However, we do treat Haiku 5.5 as meeting our CB-1 and Autonomy-1 thresholds

claim: Haiku 5.5 does not push the capability frontier set by Claude Opus 5.5 and Anthropic has high confidence it is less capable than Claude Opus 5, so the CB section reports only automated evaluations (no expert red-teaming, uplift trials, or human-participant evaluations).
quote: Claude Haiku 5.5 does not push the capability frontier set by Claude Opus 5.5, and we have high confidence it is less capable than Claude Opus 5. ... We did not conduct expert red-teaming sessions, uplift trials

claim: BioMysteryBench has been deprecated and removed from Anthropic's life sciences evaluation panel as of this release; the LatchBio Bioinformatics suite (SpatialBench Verified, SingleCellBench) is cross-referenced in its place.
quote: As of this model release, BioMysteryBench has been deprecated and removed from our panel of Life Sciences capabilities evaluations. In its place, we now cross-reference the LatchBio Bioinformatics suite

claim: On the 350-question multimodal virology (VCT) set, accuracy data labels are Haiku 5.5 0.48, Sonnet 5 0.43, Opus 5 0.55, Mythos 5.1 0.58, Opus 5.5 0.59, Sonnet 5.5 0.58, against a human expert baseline of 0.221; Haiku 4.5 is not shown.
quote: Figure 2.2.2.A bar labels: Claude Sonnet 5 0.43, Claude Opus 5 0.55, Claude Mythos 5.1 0.58, Claude Opus 5.5 0.59, Claude Sonnet 5.5 0.58, Claude Haiku 5.5 0.48; VCT expert baseline (0.221)

claim: The 95% confidence interval for Haiku 5.5 on VCT spans approximately 0.43 to 0.53 (read from error bars), overlapping the top of Sonnet 5's interval (about 0.38 to 0.48) and the bottom of Opus 5's (about 0.50 to 0.60).
quote: Error bars are 95% confidence intervals (t-intervals) over questions. Y axis 'Accuracy' 0.0-1.0.

claim: On LatchBio Bioinformatics (both evaluations) Haiku 5.5 performed comparably to Sonnet 5 and weaker than Opus 5; on Protocols it was stronger than Sonnet 5 and weaker than Opus 5; no numbers are given in this range.
quote: Haiku 5.5 performed comparably to Sonnet 5, but remained weaker than Opus 5 on both LatchBio Bioinformatics evaluations. Similarly, it was stronger than Sonnet 5 and weaker than Opus 5 on the Protocols evaluation.

claim: Anthropic's overall CB-1 judgment is that Haiku 5.5's capabilities match or exceed Sonnet 5's but fall short of Opus 5's.
quote: On balance, Haiku 5.5’s CB-1 capabilities match or exceed those of Sonnet 5, but fall short of Opus 5’s.

claim: The black-box RNA sequence design task is a medium-horizon challenge with a baseline of 57 human participants drawn from the leading edge of the US ML-bio labor market since 2018; it has a prediction subtask and a design subtask.
quote: A medium-horizon challenge on which Dyno has evaluated 57 human participants drawn from the leading edge of the US ML-bio labor market since 2018.

claim: On RNA sequence modeling, Haiku 5.5 outperformed Sonnet 5, Opus 5, and Claude Mythos 5.1 at predicting sequence properties, but was weaker at sequence design, landing between Sonnet 5 and Opus 5.
quote: It outperformed Sonnet 5, and even Opus 5 and Claude Mythos 5.1, at predicting RNA sequence properties. However, it was weaker on sequence design, appearing between Sonnet 5 and Opus 5.

claim: Haiku 5.5 used a prediction strategy similar to Opus 5.5 (the highest-scoring model on the prediction subtask) but, unlike Opus 5.5, failed to make use of its own predictions in the harder design subtask.
quote: Haiku 5.5 and Opus 5.5 share a propensity for this method, but unlike Opus 5.5, Haiku 5.5 failed to make use of its predictions in the more challenging design subtask.

claim: Haiku 5.5 showed only minor performance gains when given prior reports in context (the in-context iteration, 'with priors' condition) on the RNA task.
quote: Similarly, it exhibited only minor performance gains on the in-context iteration (“with priors”) condition.

claim: Anthropic assesses Haiku 5.5's holistic RNA-task performance as stronger than Sonnet 5 but below Opus 5, Opus 5.5, and Mythos 5.1.
quote: we assess Haiku 5.5’s holistic performance to be stronger than Claude Sonnet 5, but below that of Claude Opus 5, Opus 5.5, and Claude Mythos 5.1.

claim: RNA 'Design score (top)' means, read from the chart, are approximately Sonnet 5 9.7, Opus 5 11.1, Mythos 5.1 11.2, Opus 5.5 11.8, Sonnet 5.5 11.5, Haiku 5.5 10.6; Haiku 5.5's mean sits at roughly the human 75th percentile line (about 10.5) and one of its attempts is an outlier near 6.7.
quote: Figure 2.2.3.1.A top-left panel: y axis 'Design score (top)' 4-14; right axis 'Human performance percentile' 50%/75%/90%/100%; horizontal line is the mean; at least seven attempts per model

claim: RNA 'Design score (median)' means, read from the chart, are approximately Sonnet 5 6.7, Opus 5 9.0, Mythos 5.1 9.2, Opus 5.5 9.7, Sonnet 5.5 9.8, Haiku 5.5 7.6; Haiku 5.5's attempts spread widely, from about 4.6 to about 9.7, the widest spread of the 5.5-family models.
quote: Figure 2.2.3.1.A top-right panel: y axis 'Design score (median)' 4-14; each point is one attempt; the horizontal line is the mean

claim: RNA 'Prediction score (all)' means (rank correlation), read from the chart, are approximately Sonnet 5 0.765, Opus 5 0.788, Mythos 5.1 0.785, Opus 5.5 0.825, Sonnet 5.5 0.786, Haiku 5.5 0.817; Haiku 5.5 is second only to Opus 5.5 and sits at about the human 100th percentile line (about 0.82).
quote: Figure 2.2.3.1.A middle-left panel: y axis 'Prediction score (all)' 0.75-0.85+; right axis human percentile 100% at ~0.82, 90% at ~0.76

claim: RNA 'Prediction score (top)' means, read from the chart, are approximately Sonnet 5 0.14, Opus 5 0.17, Mythos 5.1 0.24, Opus 5.5 0.31, Sonnet 5.5 0.17, Haiku 5.5 0.27; Haiku 5.5's attempts cluster tightly (about 0.21 to 0.31).
quote: Figure 2.2.3.1.A middle-right panel: y axis 'Prediction score (top)' 0.0-0.5; horizontal line is the mean

claim: With prior reports in context, Haiku 5.5's RNA means move only slightly (read from chart): design score (top) about 10.6 to about 11.1, design score (median) about 7.6 to about 8.5, prediction score (all) about 0.817 to about 0.808 (slightly down), prediction score (top) about 0.27 to about 0.355.
quote: Figure 2.2.3.1.B: each model shown twice, 'Base' (circles) and 'With priors' (triangles); panels Design score (top), Design score (median), Prediction score (all), Prediction score (top)

claim: With prior reports, comparators gain more than Haiku 5.5 on prediction score (top), read from chart: Opus 5 about 0.17 to about 0.525, Mythos 5.1 about 0.24 to about 0.54, Sonnet 5.5 about 0.17 to about 0.455, Opus 5.5 about 0.31 to about 0.46, Sonnet 5 about 0.14 to about 0.31, versus Haiku 5.5 about 0.27 to about 0.355.
quote: Figure 2.2.3.1.B middle-right panel: y axis 'Prediction score (top)' 0.0-0.8; circles Base, triangles With priors; horizontal line is the mean of attempts

claim: With prior reports, one Haiku 5.5 attempt scored about 1.0 on design score (median) and one about 7.3 on design score (top), the lowest with-priors points of any model in those panels (Opus 5.5 also has low with-priors outliers near 3.0 and 6.6 respectively).
quote: Figure 2.2.3.1.B top panels: y axes 'Design score (top)' and 'Design score (median)' 2-14; triangles = With priors

claim: On AAV capsid packaging prediction, Haiku 5.5's performance was highly variable, weaker than Opus 5 and closer to Sonnet 5 across conditions, though it improved on Sonnet 5 in the latter two, more informative conditions.
quote: Claude Haiku 5.5’s performance was highly variable. Across conditions, its performance was weaker than that of Opus 5 and closer to that of Claude Sonnet 5. It improved upon Sonnet 5’s performance in the latter two more informative conditions

claim: AAV packaging AUROC medians for Haiku 5.5 across the five conditions, read from the box plot (eight attempts each), are approximately 0.80 (no corpus, no PLM), 0.83 (no corpus + ESM-2), 0.81 (SwissProt), 0.79 (public AAV), 0.78 (SwissProt+AAV); Opus 5, Mythos 5.1, Opus 5.5, and Sonnet 5.5 medians all sit at roughly 0.85 to 0.86 in every condition.
quote: Figure 2.2.3.2.A: y axis 'AUROC (task 1)' 0.65-0.90; conditions 'No corpus No PLM', 'No corpus +ESM-2', 'SwissProt No PLM', 'Public AAV No PLM', 'SwissProt+AAV No PLM'; eight independent attempts per model per condition

claim: Sonnet 5's AAV AUROC medians, read from the box plot, are approximately 0.82, 0.84, 0.82, 0.74, and 0.77 across the five conditions, so Haiku 5.5 is below Sonnet 5 in the first three conditions and above it in the last two (about 0.79 vs 0.74 and 0.78 vs 0.77).
quote: Figure 2.2.3.2.A: Claude Sonnet 5 (gray) and Claude Haiku 5.5 (orange) boxes; black bar is the median

claim: Haiku 5.5's run-to-run spread on AAV prediction is far wider than the other 5.5-family models: its whiskers span roughly 0.75-0.85, 0.72-0.86, 0.78-0.85, 0.78-0.82, and 0.68-0.85 across the five conditions, and individual runs fall below the naive ESM-2 baseline (about 0.70) in the public-AAV and SwissProt+AAV conditions (points near 0.69).
quote: Figure 2.2.3.2.A: dashed line 'ESM-2 alone' at ~0.70; boxes show the distribution over eight independent attempts; points show individual runs

claim: On the AAV auto-research task, Haiku 5.5 achieved strong initial performance but did not improve significantly with additional scorer calls, which Anthropic says suggests deficits in executing coherently on long-horizon research tasks; it ended slightly above Sonnet 5 and well below Opus 5.
quote: achieved strong initial performance but did not improve significantly with additional calls to the scorer, suggesting deficits in its ability to execute coherently on long-horizon biological research tasks

claim: On AAV auto-research (n = 48 attempts, 90th-percentile validation Spearman), end-of-session values read from the chart are approximately Haiku 5.5 0.511, Sonnet 5 0.505, Sonnet 5.5 0.533, Mythos 5.1 0.538, Opus 5 0.539, Opus 5.5 0.542; the 'strongest in-distribution performance' reference line is at about 0.586 and naive ESM-2 is 0.28.
quote: Figure 2.2.3.3.A left: y axis 'Spearman correlation' 0.44-0.60, x axis 'Scorer calls' 1-50; 'Naive ESM-2 achieved a Spearman correlation of 0.28'

claim: Haiku 5.5's auto-research trendline jumps from about 0.44 to about 0.50 within the first roughly 5 scorer calls, then is essentially flat (about 0.50 to 0.51) from call 5 through call 50, whereas Opus 5.5, Mythos 5.1, Opus 5, and Sonnet 5.5 keep climbing after about call 13-27 to about 0.53-0.54.
quote: Figure 2.2.3.3.A left panel trendlines; caption: 'We found that our more capable models rapidly improved using only a small number of scorer calls.'

claim: The cumulative fraction of auto-research attempts reaching a Spearman correlation of 0.52 by 50 scorer calls, read from the chart, is approximately Haiku 5.5 0.06, Sonnet 5 0.00, Sonnet 5.5 0.33, Opus 5 0.35, Mythos 5.1 0.35, Opus 5.5 0.58; Haiku 5.5's first success appears at about call 32 versus about call 12 for Opus 5.5.
quote: Figure 2.2.3.3.A right: y axis 'Fraction of attempts at or above a Spearman correlation of 0.52' 0.0-0.6, x axis 'Scorer calls' 1-50

claim: Anthropic's CB conclusion ranks Haiku 5.5 as an improvement over Sonnet 5, below Opus 5, and well below Mythos 5.1, Sonnet 5.5, and Opus 5.5.
quote: We estimate Claude Haiku 5.5’s capabilities to be an improvement over Claude Sonnet 5, but it remains below the level of Claude Opus 5, and well below the level of Claude Mythos 5.1, Sonnet 5.5, and Opus 5.5.

claim: Anthropic states Haiku 5.5 exhibited a relative deficit in the reasoning required to succeed on complex, iterative tasks (examples: the AAV autoresearch task and the RNA sequence design subtask).
quote: In particular, it exhibited a relative deficit in the reasoning required to succeed on complex, iterative tasks, such as the AAV autoresearch task and RNA sequence design subtask.

claim: Anthropic judges these shortcomings limit Haiku 5.5's effectiveness at substituting for scarce human expertise and strategic judgment in complex, open-ended, difficult-to-verify research.
quote: these shortcomings limit the model’s effectiveness at substituting for the scarce human expertise and strategic judgment required to pursue complex, open-ended, and difficult-to-verify research

claim: Because of the CB findings, Haiku 5.5 is released with the same safeguards deployed for Sonnet 5 and Opus 5 rather than the broader dual-use research-biology classifiers used for Opus 5.5.
quote: we are releasing Haiku 5.5 with the same safeguards we deployed for Sonnet 5 and Opus 5, rather than the broader dual-use research biology classifiers used for Opus 5.5.

claim: Autonomy threat model 1 (misaligned AI in high-stakes settings) is applicable to Haiku 5.5, with risk judged to remain at the 'low' level assessed in the August 2026 Risk Report.
quote: Autonomy threat model 1 is applicable to Claude Haiku 5.5, as it is to many of our previous AI models. ... the level of risk under this threat model remains at the “low” level assessed in our August 2026 Risk Report.

claim: Autonomy threat model 2 (automated R&D) is not applicable to Haiku 5.5; Anthropic finds Haiku 5.5 broadly much less capable than Claude Opus 5.5 across a variety of tasks relevant to AI R&D.
quote: Autonomy threat model 2 is not applicable to Haiku 5.5. We find that Haiku 5.5 is, broadly, much less capable than Claude Opus 5.5 across a variety of tasks relevant to AI R&D.

claim: Haiku 5.5's Anthropic ECI (AECI) is 167.11 versus 174.56 for Claude Opus 5.5, which the card calls 'much lower'.
quote: Claude Haiku 5.5’s AECI of 167.11 was much lower than Claude Opus 5.5’s score of 174.56.

claim: Other AECI values read from the chart (no data labels) are approximately Sonnet 5.5 172, Mythos 5.1 172.5, Opus 5 169, Mythos 5 168.5, Mythos Preview 165.5, Opus 4.6 157, Opus 4.5 152, Sonnet 4.5 148; Haiku 5.5 at 167.11 therefore sits a little below Opus 5 and Mythos 5 and above Mythos Preview. Haiku 4.5 is not plotted.
quote: Figure 2.3.2.A 'Anthropic ECI over time': y axis 'Anthropic ECI' 120-180, x axis 'Model release date'; legend Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Haiku 5.5, Previous frontier Claude models

claim: Haiku 5.5's 95% global confidence interval on AECI spans roughly 161.5 to 173 (read from the thin black error bar), overlapping the intervals of Opus 5, Mythos 5, Sonnet 5.5, and Mythos 5.1.
quote: Thin black error bars are 95% CI over 100 IRT refits, each on a random 80% subsample of benchmarks (global error).

claim: The AECI chart's two frontier trend fits are labeled 16.2 points/yr with a fitted +7.3 jump at Claude Mythos Preview, and 15.3 points/yr with a fitted breakpoint at Sep 2025 to 26.1/yr (1.70x slope change); the scale is anchored at Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024) = 130.
quote: Frontier trend 16.2/yr, fitted +7.3 jump at Claude Mythos Preview; Frontier trend 15.3/yr, fitted breakpoint at Sep 2025 -> 26.1/yr (1.70x slope change)

claim: AECI is powered by internal benchmark results, so its scores are not directly comparable to Epoch's public ECI leaderboard.
quote: Our version of this metric, the Anthropic ECI (AECI), is powered by internal benchmark results, so scores are not directly comparable to Epoch’s public ECI leaderboard.

claim: Anthropic concludes Haiku 5.5 does not cross the Autonomy-2 threshold because it is much less capable than Opus 5.5 (which also did not cross it) and does not push the capability frontier.
quote: As Claude Haiku 5.5 is much less capable than Opus 5.5 and does not push the capability frontier, we draw the same conclusion in this case.

claim: Anthropic notes that a less capable model could still pose higher alignment risk if it is better at deceiving users or more prone to harmful actions, so Haiku 5.5 (meeting Autonomy-1) was re-assessed against the alignment threat model.
quote: a less capable model could still pose a higher risk of taking misaligned actions in high-stakes settings if it is better at deceiving users or exhibits more concerning behaviors

claim: On the covert capabilities evaluations (detailed in Section 6.4.2, outside this range), Haiku 5.5 performed well below other recent models.
quote: On our covert capabilities evaluations described in Section 6.4.2 of this system card, Haiku 5.5 performed well below other recent models.

claim: Anthropic does not believe any observation about Haiku 5.5's alignment properties in Section 6 implies higher risk than other recent Claude models; the 'expected harm from known misalignment is low' claim is unchanged.
quote: We do not believe that any of the observations about Haiku 5.5’s alignment properties presented in Section 6 imply a higher risk than that posed by other recent Claude models.

claim: The strength of alignment-assessment evidence for Haiku 5.5 is somewhat lower than for Claude Mythos 5, because Haiku 5.5 is more recent and has seen less internal usage than Mythos 5 had at the time of the August 2026 Risk Report.
quote: somewhat lower than that presented for Claude Mythos 5 in the August 2026 Risk Report, because Haiku 5.5 is a more recent model and has seen less internal usage than Claude Mythos 5 had at the time of that report

claim: Anthropic's overall assessment is that the risk of catastrophic harm from misalignment of Haiku 5.5 is 'low', the same level set in the August 2026 Risk Report (which had been raised to 'low' after incident disclosures about model behavior in cybersecurity evaluations).
quote: our overall assessment is that the risk of catastrophic harm caused by misalignment of Claude Haiku 5.5 is also low.

claim: Haiku 5.5 is described as not a frontier model but a relatively significant step up in cyber capabilities over Haiku 4.5; across the cyber suite it significantly outperformed Haiku 4.5 but fell short of Opus 5.5, Mythos 5.1, and Opus 5.
quote: Across our evaluation suite, Haiku 5.5 significantly outperformed Haiku 4.5 but fell short of results achieved by Opus 5.5, Claude Mythos 5.1, and even Opus 5.

claim: All cyber capability results in Section 3.3 were obtained with cyber safeguards off, via the API, reflecting the capability available to certain users through the Cyber Verification Program rather than default deployed behavior.
quote: All capability evaluation results reported in Section 3.3 were obtained by evaluating Claude models with cyber safeguards off, via the API.

claim: Many cyber evaluation harnesses were rewritten since August 2026 and older models were re-evaluated, so comparator numbers in this card differ from those in earlier system cards.
quote: Many of our harnesses for evaluation runs have been rewritten since August 2026. In those cases, all older models were reevaluated to maintain consistency across models, resulting in numbers that are different from those published in previous system cards

claim: Because Haiku 5.5 relatively lacks advanced cybersecurity capabilities, its cyber safeguards trigger on significantly less activity than other recent releases; blocked security professionals are pointed to the Cyber Verification Program.
quote: Given the relative lack of advanced cybersecurity capabilities, our cyber safeguards for Claude Haiku 5.5 trigger on significantly less activity than other recent releases.

claim: ExploitBench decomposes exploitation into 16 capability flags in five tiers over 41 V8 vulnerabilities from 2024 onward, with five trials per vulnerability, a 300-turn budget, and two arms: plain (single uninterrupted attempt) and AutoNudge (harness injects a keep-trying prompt if the model voluntarily stops short of the budget without full code execution).
quote: In the AutoNudge arm, if the model voluntarily stopped short of the budget without reaching full code execution, the harness injected a keep-trying prompt into the same conversation and let it continue.

claim: On ExploitBench, Haiku 5.5 scored a mean of 5.15 capability flags (Cap% 38%) in the plain arm and 6.56 flags (Cap% 49%) in the AutoNudge arm, a gain of 1.41 flags from being nudged to keep trying after it voluntarily stopped.
quote: Haiku 5.5 scored a mean of 5.15 capability flags, for a Cap% of 38% across ExploitBench’s 41 V8 environments in the plain arm. In the AutoNudge arm, it averaged 6.56 flags, for a Cap% of 49%.

claim: Across plain and AutoNudge runs, Haiku 5.5 achieved full arbitrary code execution 1.0% of the time (4 of 410 runs) on ExploitBench.
quote: Claude Haiku 5.5 achieved full arbitrary code execution 1.0% of the time (4/410).

claim: ExploitBench AutoNudge mean capability score (0-16), from chart data labels: Haiku 4.5 2.06, Haiku 5.5 6.56, Sonnet 5.5 11.53, Mythos 5.1 12.55, Opus 5.5 14.15.
quote: Figure 3.3.1.A 'AutoNudge mean' bar labels: Claude Haiku 4.5 2.06, Claude Mythos 5.1 12.55, Claude Opus 5.5 14.15, Claude Sonnet 5.5 11.53, Claude Haiku 5.5 6.56

claim: ExploitBench AutoNudge Cap% (capability flags captured), from chart data labels: Haiku 4.5 14, Haiku 5.5 49, Sonnet 5.5 80, Mythos 5.1 83, Opus 5.5 91.
quote: Figure 3.3.1.A 'AutoNudge cap rate' bar labels: 14 (Haiku 4.5), 83 (Mythos 5.1), 91 (Opus 5.5), 80 (Sonnet 5.5), 49 (Haiku 5.5)

claim: ExploitBench full arbitrary-code-execution exploits out of 410 runs (plain plus AutoNudge), from chart data labels: Haiku 4.5 0, Haiku 5.5 4, Sonnet 5.5 178, Mythos 5.1 221, Opus 5.5 301.
quote: Figure 3.3.1.A 'Full ACEs' bar labels: 0 (Haiku 4.5), 221 (Mythos 5.1), 301 (Opus 5.5), 178 (Sonnet 5.5), 4 (Haiku 5.5); 'sum of arbitrary code execution achieved across all 410 runs'

claim: The ExploitBench results were obtained with all cyber safeguards off but escape classifiers and other safety measures enabled, using the authors' static uniform harness rather than a native harness, so they may not be comparable to public leaderboard entries.
quote: These results are obtained with all cyber safeguards turned off but with escape classifiers and other safety measures enabled. ... We report results using the static, uniform harness provided by the authors rather than a native harness.

claim: CyScenarioBench (by Irregular) measures orchestration of multi-stage operations over long horizons and is designed to surface failure modes such as context drift, incorrect branching choices, dead-end planning, and inadequate troubleshooting; Anthropic ran a 10-challenge subset.
quote: This design surfaces failure modes that only emerge over long horizons—such as context drift, incorrect branching choices, dead-end planning, and inadequate troubleshooting

claim: On CyScenarioBench (long-horizon multi-stage orchestration), Haiku 5.5 completed 3.3% of challenges versus Haiku 4.5 0%, Sonnet 5 0.7%, Sonnet 5.5 46.1%, Mythos 5.1 61.7%, and Opus 5.5 67.6%.
quote: Haiku 5.5 completed 3.3% of all challenges, a slight improvement over Claude Sonnet 5’s 0.7% and Claude Haiku 4.5’s 0%. By comparison, Claude Sonnet 5.5 completed 46.1% of the tasks, Claude Mythos 5.1 completed 61.7%, and Claude Opus 5.5 completed 67.6%.

claim: The Haiku 5.5 CyScenarioBench result came from a pre-release snapshot that Anthropic assesses to be very similar in capability to the released model.
quote: For Claude Haiku 5.5, CyScenarioBench was run on a pre-release snapshot that we assess to be very similar in capability to the released model.

claim: The CyScenarioBench chart's data labels match the text (Haiku 4.5 0.0%, Sonnet 5 0.7%, Mythos 5.1 61.7%, Opus 5.5 67.6%, Sonnet 5.5 46.1%, Haiku 5.5 3.3%); it was run with cyber mitigations off, and Opus 5 is not shown.
quote: Figure 3.3.2.A bar labels: 0.0%, 0.7%, 61.7%, 67.6%, 46.1%, 3.3%; y axis 'Overall solve rate (%, averaged across 10 challenges)'; 'This evaluation was run with our cyber mitigations turned off.'

claim: The Binary Exploitation Benchmark (formerly OSS-Fuzz) measures unguided vulnerability discovery with no hints, starting from a single entry-point function, over 831 entrypoints in 228 projects, scored on a five-step ladder from memory safety crash (0.2) to control-flow hijack (1.0).
quote: The model gets no hints about where a vulnerability may be. The 831 entrypoints span 228 projects from Google’s OSS-Fuzz corpus. A trial is scored on a five-step ladder from memory safety crash (0.2) through control-flow hijack (1.0).

claim: On the Binary Exploitation Benchmark, control-flow hijacks produced were Haiku 5.5 3, Haiku 4.5 0, Sonnet 5 3, Sonnet 5.5 50, Mythos 5.1 81, Opus 5.5 106.
quote: Claude Haiku 5.5 produced 3 control-flow hijacks. By comparison, Claude Mythos 5.1 produced 81 control-flow hijacks, Claude Opus 5.5 produced 106, Claude Sonnet 5.5 produced 50, Claude Sonnet 5 produced 3, and Claude Haiku 4.5 produced 0.

claim: Unguided vulnerability identification (Pass@1, % of 831 challenges reaching at least a memory safety bug), from chart data labels: Haiku 4.5 5.4%, Sonnet 5 55.2%, Haiku 5.5 58.2%, Sonnet 5.5 85.8%, Mythos 5.1 88.3%, Opus 5.5 91.1%.
quote: Figure 3.3.3.A 'Vulnerability identification' bar labels: 5.4% (Haiku 4.5), 55.2% (Sonnet 5), 88.3% (Mythos 5.1), 91.1% (Opus 5.5), 85.8% (Sonnet 5.5), 58.2% (Haiku 5.5); y axis 'Pass@1 (% of challenges)'

claim: In the stacked vulnerability-identification bar, the share of challenges where Haiku 5.5 progressed beyond a bare memory-safety bug (write primitive or higher) is roughly 23%, versus roughly 20% for Sonnet 5, 43% for Sonnet 5.5, 44% for Mythos 5.1, and 48% for Opus 5.5 (read from segment boundaries; segment shades are hard to separate).
quote: Figure 3.3.3.A legend: Control-flow hijack (1.0), Write-where (0.8), Pointer control (0.6), Write primitive (0.4), Memory safety bug (0.2)

claim: Anthropic characterizes Haiku 5.5 as much improved over Haiku 4.5 and a bit over Sonnet 5 in vulnerability identification, a modest improvement over Haiku 4.5 and equal to Sonnet 5 in exploit development, and not on the level of Mythos 5.1 or Opus 5.5.
quote: Claude Haiku 5.5 is a modest improvement over Claude Haiku 4.5 and the same as Claude Sonnet 5 in exploit development. It is a step up in vulnerability detection over Claude Haiku 4.5, and on par with Claude Sonnet 5.

claim: ExploitGym comprises 869 real-world vulnerability instances (502 userspace, 181 V8, 186 Linux kernel); the agent gets vulnerable source, build config, a proof-of-vulnerability input, and a container, and must achieve code execution and read a secret flag stored outside its authorized scope.
quote: The benchmark comprises 869 instances of real-world vulnerabilities across three domains: 502 userspace targets ... 181 targets in Chrome’s V8 JavaScript engine, and 186 Linux kernel targets.

claim: ExploitGym successful exploits out of 869 under 2-hour / 6-hour wall-clock budgets, from chart data labels: Haiku 5.5 79 / 82, Sonnet 5 25 / 51, Opus 5 171 / 191, Sonnet 5.5 205 / 231, Mythos 5.1 203 / 264, Opus 5.5 289 / 300; Haiku 4.5 is not shown.
quote: Figure 3.3.4.A bar labels (2 hours, 6 hours): Claude Sonnet 5 25, 51; Claude Opus 5 171, 191; Claude Mythos 5.1 203, 264; Claude Opus 5.5 289, 300; Claude Sonnet 5.5 205, 231; Claude Haiku 5.5 79, 82

claim: Tripling the ExploitGym wall-clock budget from 2 to 6 hours added only 3 exploits for Haiku 5.5 (79 to 82), the smallest gain of any model shown; Sonnet 5 gained 26, Opus 5 gained 20, Mythos 5.1 gained 61, Opus 5.5 gained 11, and Sonnet 5.5 gained 26 (differences computed from the chart's data labels).
quote: Bars show the number of successful exploits using the given vulnerability under two-hour and six-hour wall-clock budgets.

claim: Anthropic states Haiku 5.5 outperformed Sonnet 5 on ExploitGym but remained well below the other Claude 5.5-family models; each success is verified by an agent judge to confirm the intended vulnerability was used.
quote: Claude Haiku 5.5 outperformed Claude Sonnet 5 on ExploitGym but remained well below the other Claude 5.5-family models. ... each successful exploit is verified by an agent judge to confirm it uses the intended vulnerability.

claim: ExploitGym tasks were evaluated with ASLR, stack canaries, KASLR, and (except for V8 sandbox-escape tasks) the V8 heap sandbox disabled, with kernel targets keeping SMEP/SMAP enabled.
quote: We evaluate all tasks with ASLR, stack canaries, KASLR, and (except for V8 sandbox-escape tasks) the V8 heap sandbox disabled; kernel targets keep SMEP/SMAP enabled.
